holidays.name: National Coffee Day
holidays.description: Coffee lovers get a day to honor the humble bean. Cafés hand out free or discounted cups, and the rest of us have a perfect excuse to refill the mug a third time before noon.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial American observance that has been celebrated on September 29 for years. Coffee shops and roasters have embraced it, and it is separate from International Coffee Day on October 1.
holidays.funFact: Coffee beans are really the seeds of a cherry-like fruit. Legend says an Ethiopian goatherd named Kaldi discovered coffee after noticing his goats frolicking energetically after nibbling the berries.

holidays.name: National Biscotti Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates the crunchy, twice-baked Italian cookie that was practically invented for dunking. Grab a cup of coffee or a glass of sweet wine and dip away. Almond, anise, chocolate-dipped and pistachio versions are all welcome.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It fits neatly alongside National Coffee Day, since the two treats make an ideal pair.
holidays.funFact: The word biscotti comes from the Latin 'bis coctus', meaning 'twice cooked'. Baking the dough twice dries it out so thoroughly that the cookies keep for weeks, which made them handy travel food for Roman legions and sailors.
